title: Dominican Republic ties WBC HR record with walk-off blast that ousts Korea
content:
MIAMI — The party just won’t stop for the Dominican Republic at the World Baseball Classic.

Austin Wells crushed a first-pitch cutter in the bottom of the seventh inning to walk off Korea via mercy rule, 10-0, in Friday’s quarterfinal at loanDepot park. It was the Dominican Republic’s 14th homer of the tournament, tying a World Baseball Classic record previously held by the 2009 Mexico team.

Dominican Republic dominated the offensive categories in pool play. It led the tournament in home runs, runs scored, batting average, on-base percentage and slugging percentage. Yet, it’s their emphatic home run celebrations that have stolen the show. Their extraordinary bat flips and epic home run trots have ignited the crowds. It began with Junior Caminero’s go-ahead two-run homer against Nicaragua in Game 1 of pool play — Caminero’s helmet fell off as he sprinted around the bases before he leapt in the air and celebrated with the Dominican dugout down the entire third-base line.

The festivities continued from there. Dominican Republic slugged four homers in its matchup against Venezuela on Wednesday, with Juan Soto, Ketel Marte, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Fernando Tatis Jr. leaving the yard. Each reaction somehow outdid the one prior, with Tatis delivering the bat flip of the ages after smoking a three-run homer in the fourth inning that eventually sealed the game.

Manager Albert Pujols, who knows a thing or two about hitting home runs, has said throughout the tournament how much he’s enjoyed watching his players react — and how their energy is unique to their culture.

“I just don’t think you can,” Pujols said Friday when asked how MLB could replicate some of the Dominican Republic’s energy. “That’s in our blood, that’s in our DNA. That’s how we play baseball. That responsibility that we have wearing this jersey, especially representing our country — the culture, the attitude, the way the guys go about it — you’re born with that, and sometimes, that’s even harder to teach.”

Wells, Caminero, Tatis, Soto, Guerrero and Oneil Cruz have homered twice this tournament, with Marte and Julio Rodríguez also connecting. Still, even with all the power, the Dominican Republic could have some competition. Team Italy, the top seed from Pool B after upsetting Team USA, smacked 12 home runs in pool play — including three from Vinnie Pasquantino in Wednesday’s pool play game against Mexico. Italy will play Puerto Rico in a quarterfinal matchup Saturday night in Houston.

Dominican Republic will advance to the semifinal round Sunday against the winner of the United States and Canada.
